about.title: Corte Madera Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Corte Madera is a small town, but its roads carry a lot of regional traffic. US-101 slices through town alongside local routes like Tamalpais Drive and Paradise Drive, and public records show dozens of injury collisions here every year, many clustering on Wednesday evenings when commute and errand traffic overlap. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter. Photos, witness contacts, and vehicle damage can disappear or get repaired before you've had time to think it through. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who takes it from there, typically on a contingency basis, meaning you owe nothing unless they recover money for you. Our role ends once that connection is made; the attorney and you decide how to move forward from there.

whyChoose.title: Why Reach Out Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government entity like Caltrans or Marin County is involved. Waiting to sort out fault can quietly cost you your case.

items.title: Fault Isn't All-or-Nothing Here
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if an insurer tries to pin partial blame on you, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can push back on inflated fault claims before they get baked into a settlement offer.

items.title: Don't Give a Recorded Statement Yet
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement early, often before you know the full extent of your injuries. Speaking with an attorney first helps make sure nothing you say gets used later to minimize what you're owed, especially since California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering.

items.question: Why do so many crashes happen on Wednesdays around 5-7 p.m. in Corte Madera?
items.answer: Public crash records show reported collisions in Corte Madera tend to cluster on Wednesday evenings, likely tied to commute traffic mixing with local errands near US-101 and Tamalpais Drive. This is simply a pattern in the data, not a judgment about any particular road. If your crash happened during this window, it may help establish traffic conditions at the time.

items.question: What if my accident happened on US-101 and involved a government vehicle or road defect?
items.answer: Claims involving a government entity, like Caltrans for a state highway issue, often carry a much shorter deadline — sometimes as little as six months to file a claim notice. This is very different from the standard two-year window for typical car accident claims. An attorney can help you figure out quickly which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: Do I have to talk to the other driver's insurance company right away?
items.answer: No, and it's usually better if you don't give a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements, made before you know the full scope of your injuries, to reduce what they later offer. An independent attorney can communicate with the insurer on your behalf.
